title: Slow-cooker beef cheeks in red wine
subtitle: Eight hours of low heat, a sauce that coats the spoon
excerpt: Beef cheeks braised in red wine and stock until they yield to a spoon. Set up in the morning, ready by dinner with almost no hands-on time.
sourceNotes: Braised beef cheeks are a staple of French brasserie cooking. The method draws on classic French braise technique found in Escoffier, Le Guide Culinaire (1903) and Richard Olney, Simple French Food (1974).

recipe.freezeNotes: Cool completely, transfer to airtight containers, and freeze for up to 3 months. Defrost overnight in the fridge and reheat gently with a splash of stock.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: The dish improves overnight. Reheat covered on the hob over low heat, adding a little water if the sauce has tightened.

glossaryTerms.definition: A slow-cook method where meat is browned in fat first, then cooked covered in a small amount of liquid until the fibres soften and the cooking liquid thickens.

content.text: Beef cheeks are one of the most forgiving cuts in the slow cooker. The muscle that works constantly in a living animal becomes very tender after eight hours of gentle heat, yielding to a spoon and holding its shape just long enough to serve. This is economical cooking: an inexpensive cut, a long unattended day, a result that tastes like far more effort.

: brown the meat in a hot pan first, then transfer to the slow cooker with wine, stock, and aromatics. The browning adds depth that long cooking alone cannot give. Eight hours on the low setting does the rest.
Serve with mashed potatoes or soft polenta. The sauce is rich enough that it needs something to absorb it.

Pat {{ox-cheek}} of beef cheeks dry with kitchen paper and season all over with salt and pepper. Heat {{olive-oil}} of olive oil in a frying pan over high heat. Sear the cheeks in batches, 3 to 4 minutes per side, until deeply browned on both surfaces. Transfer to the slow cooker.

Reduce the heat in the frying pan to medium. Add {{onion}} chopped onion, {{carrot}} chopped carrots, and {{celery}} chopped celery stalks. Cook for 5 minutes until slightly softened. Add {{garlic}} of crushed garlic and {{tomato-puree}} of tomato puree; stir for 1 minute.

Pour {{red-wine}} of red wine into the pan. Let it bubble for 1 minute, scraping up any browned bits from the base. Pour the wine and vegetables into the slow cooker over the cheeks. Add {{stock-beef}} of beef stock and {{tinned-tomatoes}} of tinned tomatoes. Tuck in {{thyme}} of thyme and {{bay-leaves}} of bay.

Set the slow cooker to LOW. Cook for 7 to 8 hours. The cheeks are ready when they offer almost no resistance when pressed and the sauce has turned a deep, dark colour. Discard the thyme stalks and bay leaves.

Lift the cheeks out carefully and set aside. If the sauce looks thin, pour it into a wide pan and reduce over high heat for 5 to 10 minutes until it coats the back of a spoon. Return the cheeks to warm through before serving.

rows.symptom: The cheeks are still tough after 8 hours
rows.cause: Slow cookers vary in their actual temperature on the low setting. Older or less powerful models may not reach a high enough temperature to break down collagen.
rows.fix: Switch to the high setting for 1 to 2 more hours. This cut cannot overcook into dryness, only into greater tenderness.

rows.cause: Slow cookers trap steam so liquids do not reduce during cooking. The volume of wine and stock may be more than the vegetables can absorb.
rows.fix: Pour the sauce into a wide saucepan and boil over high heat until reduced to a coating consistency, about 5 to 10 minutes.

rows.cause: The red wine has not cooked out fully, or the wine used was very acidic.
rows.fix: A small knob of butter stirred in at the end will round the flavour. Next time, allow the wine an extra minute in the pan before adding it to the slow cooker.

rows.symptom: The meat looks dry on top but is soft underneath
rows.cause: The cheeks were sitting above the liquid level for the final hours of cooking.
rows.fix: Baste the cheeks partway through if possible, or ensure the liquid covers the meat at least halfway before starting. This is cosmetic and does not affect the eating quality.

content.text: Beef cheeks improve with a night in the fridge. Cool the dish, then refrigerate uncovered until cold, cover, and store for up to 3 days. Reheat gently on the hob. To freeze, portion into airtight containers and freeze for up to 3 months. Defrost overnight in the fridge.

Braised beef cheeks appear on bistro menus across France and in the winter repertoire of British home cooks who have discovered the cut. The slow cooker makes the technique accessible: what once required a heavy casserole dish and a low oven can now be set up in the morning. It pairs well with anything starchy, from buttered noodles to roasted root vegetables.
